Another MedlinePlus snippet also shows the converse exception: a fetus with an X chromosome carrying the SRY gene “will develop as a male despite not having a Y chromosome” [d12].  
So the retrieved evidence supports a more nuanced answer: the Y chromosome is often important in male development, but it is not an exclusive or absolute determinant of only male gender [d1][d12][d11].
